title: Tignes Val d'Isère | Linked ski areas | Snow Catchers
description: How Tignes and Val d'Isère fit together across the Tovière and Bellevarde ridge, which base reaches which side, how the snow changes with height, what the single area pass costs, and what the area is like for boarders, families, food and evenings.

hero.lead: Tignes and Val d'Isère share the head of the Isère valley, joined over the ridge of Tovière and Bellevarde into one area that the operator puts at {{f:op_km}} of piste. Its lifts climb from Les Brévières at {{f:op_low}} to the Grande Motte cable car at {{f:op_high}}. Tignes was built for skiing after its old village vanished under the Chevril reservoir in {{f:tg_flooded}}, and in {{f:vi_olympic}} Val d'Isère staged the Olympic men's downhill on the Face de Bellevarde.

paras: Tignes fills the upper bowl of its valley, from Les Brévières and Tignes 1800 near the Chevril dam up to Le Lac, Le Lavachet and Val Claret around the lake, with the Grande Motte glacier above them. Val d'Isère lies over the ridge to the east, strung out from La Daille through the village to Le Fornet, with Bellevarde and Solaise on either side of it. Lifts from both resorts reach the ridge between Tovière and Bellevarde, and in the map data a skier from Val Claret reaches La Daille in one lift ride and comes back in one.

The link is broad. In the model no single lift closure separates the two resorts, and the worst closures add lift rides rather than cut journeys. Closing the Olympique or the Solaise gondola in the centre of Val d'Isère adds {{f:olympique_extra}} lift rides in total across the journeys between sectors, and closing the Tommeuses chair, the main way up from La Daille to Tignes, adds {{f:tommeuses_extra}}.

Le Fornet is the exception. Its lifts climb to the Pissaillas glacier, but the only lift out of the sector towards the rest of the area is the Leissières chair to Solaise. If it stops, Le Fornet can still be reached on skis but none of the other {{f:leissieres_cut|w}} sectors can be reached from it by lift.

areas.note: From the OpenStreetMap lift and piste data (snapshot 24 October 2026) with heights from the Copernicus 90 m elevation model. Green and blue is the share of mapped piste length; drag lifts include platters and T bars as a share of the main lifts. paras: The operator counts {{f:runs_total}} runs: {{f:runs_green}} green, {{f:runs_blue}} blue, {{f:runs_red}} red and {{f:runs_black}} black. skiresort.com measures {{f:F000084}} of the piste as easy, {{f:F000085}} as intermediate and {{f:F000086}} as difficult, the highest difficult share of the four Savoie areas on this site.

Green and blue reach every sector in the map data, but the way round can be long. Between the centres of the two resorts the easy routes cost at most one extra lift ride, while Solaise and Le Fornet are another matter: from Tignes Le Lac, Le Fornet takes {{m:easy.le-lac.le-fornet|w}} lift rides on green and blue against {{m:all.le-lac.le-fornet|w}} with every run allowed.

Black runs matter more here than in the other big Savoie areas. Coming back into Tignes Le Lac and Les Brévières from Val d'Isère, the fewest lift rides use a black run, and staying on reds costs one more ride: from the village of Val d'Isère, Tignes Le Lac takes {{m:all.val-disere.le-lac|w}} lift rides with a black and {{m:red.val-disere.le-lac|w}} without.

The steepest skiing is on the Val d'Isère side. The Face de Bellevarde, the Olympic downhill of {{f:vi_olympic}}, runs from the Rocher de Bellevarde to the village, and the Oreiller-Killy red drops about {{f:ok_drop}} over just over {{f:ok_len}} to La Daille. On the Tignes side the Grande Motte glacier runs fall about {{f:gm_drop}} to Val Claret when they are fully open.

paras: Most of the skiing starts high. Tignes Le Lac and Val Claret have their lowest lifts at {{f:lo.le-lac}} and {{f:lo.val-claret}}, and on the elevation model the Grande Motte lifts start at {{f:lo.grande-motte}} and climb to {{f:hi.grande-motte}}. The low ground is limited to Les Brévières, La Daille and the village of Val d'Isère, whose lowest lifts start between {{f:lo.brevieres|n}} and {{f:lo.val-disere}}.

The weather model behind the snowfall figures covers the whole area with one grid cell, so it cannot tell Tignes from Val d'Isère, but it shows plainly what height does. In a typical season between 1991 and 2020, about {{f:F000105}} of snow fell at 1,600 m, {{f:s2100}} at 2,100 m and {{f:s2600}} at 2,600 m.

The lower slopes have lost the most. At 1,600 m the typical season fell from {{f:s1600_old}} in 1961 to 1990 to {{f:F000105}} in 1991 to 2020, and four of the last five seasons sat in the lowest third of the 76 year record. At 2,600 m the fall was smaller, from {{f:s2600_old}} to {{f:s2600}}, though three of the last five seasons were that poor.

Height still sets the calendar. Tignes opens on {{f:open_tignes|dm}}, a week before the link to Val d'Isère on {{f:open_linked|dm}}, and the whole area runs to {{f:close_linked|dm}}, later than the linked areas of Les 3 Vallées and Paradiski. The model gives snowfall rather than depth on the ground, and measured depths from weather stations are still being collected.

access.h2: Getting there and choosing a base
paras: By the fastest road, Geneva airport is {{f:gva_brev}} from Les Brévières and {{f:gva_fornet}} from Le Fornet, Lyon airport {{f:lys_min|n}} to {{f:lys_max}} and Chambéry {{f:cmf_min|n}} to {{f:cmf_max}}. Every route climbs from Bourg-Saint-Maurice on the D902 past the Chevril dam, and the Col de l'Iseran beyond Val d'Isère is closed to traffic in winter, so there is no way in from the Maurienne.

Bourg-Saint-Maurice is the railway station, {{f:bsm_min|n}} to {{f:bsm_max}} from the villages by road, and the Eurostar ski service from London calls there on winter Saturdays. Regional buses run from the station to both resorts, and some long distance coaches stop at La Daille, where free shuttles run to the centre of Val d'Isère.

Tignes and Val d'Isère fall under the Loi Montagne, which from November to March requires winter tyres on all four wheels or snow chains in the car. Both resorts charge for parking in garages and car parks, while Les Brévières has a free open car park for day visitors, according to skiresort.com. Alps2Alps, a transfer company, warns that Saturday changeovers bring long queues on the single lane stretches of the D902, and advises leaving the resort many hours before a Saturday flight.
access.accessNote: Road distances are the fastest route by the OSRM router on OpenStreetMap data, without traffic or snow. The ski train as reported by Seat 61; roads and buses by Guide Ski. Winter equipment rules: Allopneus (October 2026); parking: skiresort.com; Saturday traffic: Alps2Alps (August 2026), a transfer company. 2026/27 bus timetables have not yet been checked.
basesParas: Tignes Le Lac and Val Claret are the best placed bases. From Val Claret, Val d'Isère is {{f:b.val-claret.val-disere|w}} lift rides away and a lift top above 3,000 m only {{f:b.val-claret.top3000|w}}, by the Perce-Neige funicular. From the village of Val d'Isère, Tignes Le Lac is {{f:b.val-disere.le-lac|w}} lift rides away.

Les Brévières and Le Fornet are quieter, and further from the rest of the area by lift. From Les Brévières, Val d'Isère takes {{f:b.brevieres.val-disere|w}} lift rides and Le Fornet {{f:b.brevieres.le-fornet|w}}; from Le Fornet, Tignes Le Lac takes {{f:b.le-fornet.le-lac|w}}.

chapters.h2: Riding Tignes Val d'Isère on a board
paras: Each resort keeps its own park. Tignes has its snowpark at the top of the Grattalu chair above Val Claret, with kickers, rails and boxes for beginners and intermediates and a free airbag, a halfpipe at the foot of the Lanches chair, and an expert boardercross in the same Palet sector. Val d'Isère's Val Park fills the middle of the Bellevarde bowl below the Mont Blanc chair, with kickers graded from green to black. In 2026 the Grande Motte glacier also opened for a month of summer skiing from late June, though SnowStash reports that most of it was on leftover winter snow.

Tignes keeps its off piste close to the lifts. See Tignes points to the trees off the Aiguille Percée chair above Les Brévières for days when the light goes flat, but warns that without a guide it is easy to end up stranded at the bottom. Higher up, a small bowl to the left of the Double M lift and the edges of the Grande Motte runs hold soft snow after a fall. Ski New Gen puts the Vallon de la Sache among its five favourite Tignes routes, a short hike from the chairs near the Aiguille Percée, with open ground and narrow couloirs all the way down to Les Brévières.

Val d'Isère has the better known routes. Ultimate France calls the Tour du Charvet, reached from the Grand Pré chair on Bellevarde, a good first off piste route for competent riders, and it runs through the Vanoise National Park. Above Le Fornet the Montet drag leads to the Col Pers, which the same guide rates suitable for every off piste level, and to the much steeper Pointe Pers. For poor visibility it recommends the steep, spaced trees below the Le Fornet cable car, and the Danaïdes woods above Le Laisinant offer jumps and drops between cliffs.

Drag lifts are scarce in the villages and common on the glacier. In the map data {{f:m_drags}} of the {{f:m_main}} main lifts are drags; they make up {{f:drag.grande-motte}} of the main lifts on the Grande Motte and {{f:drag.le-fornet}} in Le Fornet, against {{f:drag.val-claret}} in Val Claret. All of the terrain beyond the markers is uncontrolled, so the avalanche bulletin and a local guide come first.

paras: Tignes and Val d'Isère both carry the Famille Plus label for family resorts, and the pass is generous to the young: children under 8 ski free, and a family buying four week passes together saves {{f:family_pack}} on the total.

Tignes makes the first days easy. Free beginner lifts run at Le Lac, Le Lavachet and Val Claret, the Bollin chair at Val Claret is free, and four free sledging areas sit at Le Lac, Le Lavachet, Tignes 1800 and Les Brévières. The Expédition Cobra snow luge runs about {{f:cobra_len}} down from Palafour and is not recommended for children under 13, and passes of six days or more include unlimited entry to the Lagon pool.

Val d'Isère has a free drag to the green Savonnette run at the foot of the main snow front, Ski Tranquille slow zones at Solaise and Bellevarde, a snow garden for the youngest, and the Centre Aquasportif with a sports pool and a leisure pool. Free shuttles link La Daille, Le Fornet and Legettaz to the centre.
For a base, Tignes Le Lac has the highest share of green and blue in the map data, {{f:easy.le-lac}}, and sits one lift ride from Val Claret, La Daille and Les Brévières.

paras: Each resort has one Michelin star in the 2026 guide: Ursus in Tignes, where Clément Bouvier cooks, and La Table de l'Ours in Val d'Isère, Antoine Gras's restaurant in the Barmes de l'Ours hotel.

On the Val d'Isère side, Le Signal at the top of the Le Fornet cable car has a sun terrace, a log fire and a yurt for cold days. La Peau de Vache, halfway down La Face, is known for burgers big enough for two, and Le Refuge de Solaise serves gourmet food in a glass conservatory below the top of the Solaise gondola. Down in the village, La Baraque on the main street has live folk music and a following among locals.

In Tignes, L'Alpage des Chaudannes and Lo Soli share the top of the Chaudannes chair above Le Lac and Le Lavachet. The first serves Savoyard dishes and Savoie wines on a sun terrace, and the second offers table service alongside a self service counter. In Val Claret, La Taverne des Neiges by the Bollin and Fresse chairs looks up at the Grande Motte, and Snowcarbon recommends Le Panoramic mainly for its views.

Down in the villages, Snowcarbon recommends Le Coeur des Neiges at Le Lac for tartiflette around fire pits, Le Caveau in Val Claret for home style Savoyard cooking, and Bazurto, also in Val Claret, for Colombian cooking on a special occasion. Les Brévières has the most traditional setting, with L'Armailly in a handsome chalet, and the restaurants at the foot of its slopes fill up at lunchtime.

paras: La Folie Douce on the Daille gondola above La Daille was opened by Luc Reversade in {{f:folie_opened}}, and once enlarged it is credited with inventing open air après clubbing. Its afternoons run to live bands, DJs and cabaret until the lifts close.

In Val d'Isère, Cocorico beside the main lift by the bus turning circle keeps the afternoon going, with La Doudoune in its basement open until five in the morning, and Dick's Tea Bar in the centre, opened in {{f:dicks_opened}}, takes over late at night.

Tignes spreads its evenings between Le Lac and Val Claret. The Loop Bar at Le Lac can be skied to from the Trolles slope, and Strike, in the old bowling alley, claims to be the largest club in the Alps. In Val Claret, the Drop Zone has the biggest south facing terrace in Tignes by Iglu Ski's account, and the Melting Pot stays open until four in the morning.

The smaller villages are quieter. Le Lavachet has Le Brasero, a ski in, ski out bar with live music and burgers, and See Tignes describes the hamlet as local in feel and good for après. Les Brévières has a laid back scene built around its restaurants, and with no shuttle buses to the other villages, most people stay put once the lifts close.

fit.catches: The six day pass is the dearest of the four Savoie areas on this site, and neither resort offers a cheaper week of its own. The fewest lift rides back into Tignes Le Lac and Les Brévières from Val d'Isère use black runs, and Le Fornet depends on a single chair. Lower down, the modelled snow has thinned, with four of the last five seasons at 1,600 m in the lowest third.

compare.h2: The other large areas of Savoie
paras: Set against its neighbours, Tignes Val d'Isère is smaller than Les 3 Vallées and Paradiski, with {{f:F000080}} of piste against {{f:F000002}} and {{f:F000071}}, but it climbs highest, to {{f:F000083}}, and has the largest share of difficult piste, {{f:F000086}}.

Its day ticket matches Paradiski's at {{f:F000067}}, but its six day pass is the dearest of the four at {{f:F000068}}. In the weather model it has the least snow of the four at 1,600 m, which matters less where Tignes Le Lac and Val Claret start at {{f:lo.le-lac}} and {{f:lo.val-claret}}.

items.dd: Tignes and Val d'Isère, the two resorts on the Tignes Val d'Isère pass, split into the eight sectors that a skier meets on the ground. Sharing the pass is recorded separately from being linked by lift and piste.

A sector counts as linked only when a route of lifts and pistes reaches it in the OpenStreetMap data. Drag lifts run one way, gondolas and the two funiculars may be ridden down, and the walks from the underground Perce-Neige stations and along the Val Claret snow front are added by hand. A link is critical when closing one lift on it cuts routes that no other lift replaces. The model has not yet been checked against the official 2026/27 piste map.
Operator and measured figures are both shown and never averaged. Mapped piste from OpenStreetMap is used only to compare sectors and grades.
The four areas compared use the same source for each row, so a figure can be set against its neighbour.

method.sources: Research of 24 October 2026. Size, runs, lifts, season dates, parks and passes: Guide Ski for Tignes and for Val d'Isère, and the 2026/27 rate sheet. Measured size and grades: skiresort.com. History: Wikipedia on Tignes and Val d'Isère. Network, bases, routes and lift heights: a graph of {{f:m_lifts}} lifts and {{f:m_sections}} piste sections from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), with heights from the Copernicus 90 m elevation model via Open-Meteo. Snowfall: ERA5 reanalysis via the Open-Meteo historical weather API (CC BY 4.0). Road distances: OSRM. Facts from operators, measurements, model results and estimates are kept apart in the research files, and conflicting figures are listed above rather than averaged.
